views.label: People per day
views.hero: Facebook and Instagram each have roughly 700 times Bluesky's daily users, and TikTok about 300 times.

rows.name: Facebook
rows.basis: Last official figure, December 2023; Meta no longer reports Facebook separately. In July 2026 Zuckerberg said only that it has had "more than 2 billion daily actives for a while now".

rows.name: Instagram
rows.basis: Company-reported daily actives, Meta earnings call, July 29, 2026. Meta's own count, so broader than the mobile estimates here.

rows.name: TikTok (weak estimate)
rows.basis: TikTok publishes no global daily figure. Outside estimates run from about 0.9B to 1.1B, and they are modelled, not reported.

rows.name: Threads
rows.basis: Mobile daily users, July 2026, Similarweb estimate

rows.name: Reddit
rows.basis: Company-reported daily active uniques, Q3 2026. Includes logged-out visitors, many arriving from search, so it is broader than the app figures here.

rows.name: X
rows.basis: Mobile daily users, July 2026, Similarweb estimate. X also gets about 4.7B monthly web visits, not counted here.

rows.name: Bluesky: opened the app
rows.basis: Mobile daily users, July 2026, Similarweb estimate

rows.name: Bluesky: liked something
rows.basis: Accounts that liked at least one post on Oct 29, 2026. Measured from the network, not estimated.

rows.name: Bluesky: posted something
rows.basis: Accounts that posted on Oct 29, 2026. Measured from the network, not estimated.

views.label: People per month
views.hero: Facebook and Instagram each have nearly 300 times Bluesky's monthly users. Bluesky is about 12 times Mastodon.

rows.name: Facebook
rows.basis: Last official figure, December 2023. Meta has not reported monthly Facebook users since then, so this is nearly three years old.

rows.name: Instagram
rows.basis: Company-reported monthly users, announced by Mark Zuckerberg on September 24, 2025.

rows.name: TikTok (weak estimate)
rows.basis: TikTok publishes no regular global figure. Estimates cluster near 2B; a 2.21B figure in circulation is advertising reach, not active users.

rows.name: Threads
rows.basis: Company-reported monthly actives, Meta earnings call, July 29, 2026.

rows.name: X
rows.basis: Mobile app monthly users, June 2026, Similarweb estimate. Company figures are far higher but aren't comparable.

rows.name: Bluesky
rows.basis: Mobile app monthly users, June 2026, Similarweb estimate

rows.name: Truth Social (weak estimate)
rows.basis: Secondary compilation of a Similarweb estimate from September 2025. The company publishes no user numbers, and other estimates differ, so treat this as rough.

rows.name: Mastodon
rows.basis: Monthly active users reported by Mastodon servers, tracker read Nov 5, 2026. Servers opt in to reporting, so this is a lower bound.

views.label: Open networks, per month
views.hero: Bluesky is the largest open social network by far: about 7 times the whole fediverse, Mastodon included.

rows.name: Bluesky
rows.basis: Mobile app monthly users, June 2026, Similarweb estimate. Bluesky is run by a for-profit public benefit company, but it is built on an open protocol other apps can use.

rows.name: Fediverse, all software
rows.basis: Monthly active users across about 44,000 servers that report statistics, Nov 5, 2026. Mastodon is most of it. Reporting is opt-in, so this undercounts somewhat.

rows.name: Mastodon
rows.basis: Monthly active users reported by Mastodon servers, Nov 2026. Run as a nonprofit.

rows.name: Pixelfed
rows.basis: Monthly active users reported by Pixelfed servers, Nov 2026 (photo sharing). Another tracker put it near 100,000 in mid-2026, so treat this as uncertain.

rows.name: PeerTube
rows.basis: Monthly active users reported by PeerTube servers, Nov 2026 (video).

rows.name: Lemmy
rows.basis: Monthly active users reported by Lemmy servers, Nov 2026 (Reddit-style forums). Another tracker put it near 45,000.

rows.name: Nostr
rows.basis: Monthly active profiles, Nov 6, 2026, from one tracker; about 4,000 a day. Nostr has no central count, so estimates vary.

note: These sources count differently, so differences of a few percent mean nothing. Bluesky's figure is app users estimated from phones; fediverse figures are logged-in users reported by servers.
